the Kelch-like Echinoderm Homologue Associated Protein 1 (Kea1p)/nuclear factor-erythroid 2 related factor 2 (NF-E2 related factor 1, NRF1) system is the main mechanism for cellular defense under oxidative stress, however, the downstream stress protein response in the motor neuron (MN), which is the main target of ALS pathology is selectively decreased in the ALS model mice.
In summary, our research is concerned with
a novel therapeutic strategy of ALS by the activation of the Keap1/ Nrf2 system and its downstream stress response proteins.
the role of the Keap1/ Nrf2 system and its downstream stress response proteins in ALS pathology.
the role of the Keap1-Nrf2 pathway in the motor neuron degeneration of ALS model mice.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the Keap1/ Nrf2 system activation is not the only mechanism of the neurodegeneration in the ALS model mice, and the selective loss of downstream protective proteins in MN may be a key mechanism of neurodegeneration in ALS.
ALS MNs are vulnerable to oxidative damage, but the cellular defense system is impaired and unable to respond to the stress.

the Keap1-Nrf2 system is a critical cellular defense mechanism in ALS pathogenesis, but the selective loss of the downstream stress protein inductions in the MN could be a pivotal factor in the ALS pathogenesis.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the Keap1 and Nrf2 are not involved in MN death, but the downstream stress proteins are involved in MN death.
the MN degeneration in ALS model mice was not associated with a significant increase of downstream stress response proteins, which could be an important factor in the selective loss of MN in ALS.

the Keap1 and Nrf2 system is activated in the MN nucleus and in the glial-like cells, but the MN nucleus is not capable of activating downstream stress response proteins, which is a critical factor of ALS neurodegeneration.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the loss of downstream protective proteins such as HO1, glutathion, TRX, or HSP70 in MN could be a critical mechanism of neurodegeneration in ALS, which is not related to Keap1/Nr2 system activation.
the Nrf2 pathway is upregulated in motor neurons of the ALS model mice.
